issues.legal_issue: A later partition does not reset the commencement of limitation where the claimants had antecedent title and the opposing possession had already become adverse.
material_facts: The claimants asserted that they acquired ownership as reversioners under a registered partition deed executed after the opposing occupants had entered possession.
The claimants also asserted possession through a predecessor before his death.
The lower courts found that the opposing occupants had been in possession for decades before the partition deed and had been treating the land as their own.
issues.conclusion: The partition deed did not confer a new title or restart limitation. The relevant starting point was when the opposing occupants’ possession became adverse, and the rule concerning a reversioner’s right to recover after the death of a life tenant did not apply.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 65 of the Limitation Act, limitation for recovery based on title runs from when the defendant’s possession becomes adverse. Explanation (a) to Article 65 concerns the distinct situation in which a reversioner succeeds after a life tenant’s death. As held in Ram Kisto Mandal v. Dhankisto Mandal, a reversioner’s right in that situation rests on Hindu law and the principle that the reversioner has an expectancy rather than a title through the widow. A partition transforms joint enjoyment into separate enjoyment; it does not confer a new title because each co-sharer has antecedent title. Hanamgowda v. Irgowda supports the principle that limitation begins when possession becomes adverse, not when the claimant’s ownership right arises.

predicates.title_and_possession_suit: The claimants brought a suit seeking recovery of land on the basis of title.
predicates.claimants_relied_on_later_partition: The claimants relied on a later partition as the event by which they said they acquired ownership.
predicates.defendants_possession_became_adverse_bef: The opposing occupants’ possession had become adverse before the partition relied on by the claimants.

issues.definition: When a title-based possession suit relies on a later partition but the opposing possession had already become adverse, limitation runs from the adverse possession rather than the partition.

issues.legal_issue: Long, open, exclusive, and hostile possession, demonstrated by acts of ownership and assessed in light of the concurrent factual findings, can establish adverse possession and bar a later possession suit.
material_facts: The lower courts found that the opposing occupants had possessed the land since 1935 or, at the latest, 1941.
The occupants paid revenue assessments from 1940 and paid property taxes; their names were recorded in revenue records.
The local council permitted the occupants to build a compound wall, and the occupants built it.
The claimants’ evidence was that their predecessor had refused the occupants permission to build and that the wall was built without the claimants’ permission.
The trial and appellate courts found in favour of adverse possession and held the possession suit barred by limitation; the High Court confirmed those findings.
issues.conclusion: The opposing occupants established adverse possession, and the concurrent findings that the possession suit was barred by limitation were upheld. The Court found no reason to interfere with those findings and dismissed the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: A defendant relying on adverse possession must establish hostile intention, long and uninterrupted possession, and open exercise of exclusive ownership to the knowledge of the owner. Article 65 of the Limitation Act governs recovery of possession based on title. The Court relied on the concurrent factual findings concerning the duration and character of possession and declined to interfere with them in the appeal.

rule.if: civil_appeal_from_concurrent_adverse_possession_findings and defendants_possessed_for_decades and defendants_paid_assessments_and_taxes and defendants_were_recorded_as_occupants and defendants_built_wall_under_public_permission

predicates.civil_appeal_from_concurrent_adverse_pos: The proceeding was an appeal challenging concurrent findings that possession was adverse.
predicates.defendants_possessed_for_decades: The opposing occupants possessed the land for several decades.
predicates.defendants_paid_assessments_and_taxes: The opposing occupants paid land assessments and property taxes on the land.
predicates.defendants_were_recorded_as_occupants: The opposing occupants’ names were entered in public land records.
predicates.defendants_built_wall_under_public_permi: The opposing occupants built a compound wall after receiving permission from a local public body.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges concurrent adverse-possession findings and the opposing occupants possessed the land for decades while paying assessments and taxes, appearing in public records, and building a wall with public permission, adverse possession and the resulting limitation bar are upheld.
